notes: Main-split ABox revision of a stored fact (15 queries), kept from the earlier version (rated unlikely) and moved to the new layout, now on part_of_war (staging: functional, so a contraction of the original fact can be paired). The edit moves an individual battle from one class (battles of the American Revolutionary War) to another (battles of the War of 1812). The three determinate derived questions ask only about the war itself (its end year, its start year, and the battle under its other name Breed's Hill), never about the battle's own date: the battle's date (17 June 1775) is stored by name and is not touched by the edit, so a question about it is the background-beliefs query. The indeterminate query is that one: the century of the battle, nineteenth if its time comes from its war, eighteenth if its own date is kept. The Chinese direct question keeps the English name in brackets: three models missed the bare Chinese name (邦克山战役) in the audit, which was a naming problem, not a missing fact; the rewording is not yet re-audited. Review fixes: negation now reads "Is it true that ... not ..." and yes/no answers are lowercase; the Spanish new answer is the common name "la guerra de 1812"; the century and Madison questions (answerable from the battle's own date, which the edit leaves alone) and the Warren query (1775 is firm) are gone. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama) except those marked approximate. Related replaced 2026-11-14: 'Did the American Revolutionary War include the Battle of Bunker Hill?' was the edit's inverse with counts under 100. Now the three battles named together ('Lexington, Concord and Bunker Hill' 349 and 347 hits), tied to the edit through one bridge (Lexington and Concord belong to the Revolutionary War). The counts are for the list of the three battles, the closest exact phrase to the composed sentence.
